subject: radiology
title: Four Rs of Radiobiology, Alpha Beta Ratio and Oxygen Effect

steps.title: Repair between fractions
steps.tx: **Repair** of sublethal damage is the first R: cells mend radiation injury over hours, and splitting dose into daily fractions lets normal late responding tissues repair more completely than most tumours. That repair gap is the entire biological excuse for fractionation. It half completes in roughly one to two hours for many tissues, which is why same day fractions are spaced at least six hours apart.
steps.say: Repair of sublethal damage is the first R: cells mend radiation injury over hours, and daily fractions let normal tissues repair more completely than most tumours. That repair gap is the biological excuse for fractionation. Same day fractions are spaced at least six hours apart for it.

steps.title: Reoxygenation opens the tumour
steps.tx: **Reoxygenation** is the second R: each fraction kills the oxygenated outer tumour cells, letting previously hypoxic deeper cells move closer to vessels and oxygenate before the next fraction. Hypoxic cells resist radiation about threefold, so a single massive dose wastes itself on that resistant core. Fractionation therefore converts the tumours own geography into a conveyor that keeps feeding sensitive cells into the kill zone.
steps.say: Reoxygenation is the second R: each fraction kills oxygenated outer cells, letting hypoxic deeper cells oxygenate before the next fraction. Hypoxic cells resist radiation about threefold, so one massive dose wastes itself on that core. Fractionation keeps feeding sensitive cells into the kill zone.

steps.title: Redistribution into sensitive phases
steps.tx: **Redistribution** is the third R: cells in late S phase resist radiation while cells in G2 and mitosis die easily, and survivors redistribute around the cycle between fractions into sensitive phases. A single dose catches only the fraction of tumour sitting in a sensitive window that hour. Daily fractions repeatedly sample the cycle, so asynchronous tumours steadily present new sensitive targets while arrested normal stem cells shelter in resistant phases.

One dose catches only that hours sensitive window. Daily fractions repeatedly sample the cycle, presenting new sensitive targets.

steps.title: Repopulation fights back
steps.tx: **Repopulation** is the fourth R and the enemy inside the list: surviving tumour clonogens accelerate their division weeks into a course, replacing killed cells faster each day. Head and neck cancers repopulate at a rate costing roughly 0.6 gray per day after about four weeks, so unnecessary breaks and protracted courses surrender control. Accelerated schedules that compress treatment exist precisely to outrun this clock, at the price of fiercer acute mucosal reactions.

steps.title: Alpha beta ratio sets fraction size
steps.tx: **Alpha beta ratio** from the linear quadratic model measures fractionation sensitivity in gray: tumours and early reacting tissues sit high near 10, repairing little between fractions, while late tissues like cord sit low near 2 to 3 and are spared by small fractions. Hypofractionation exploits a low tumour ratio, prostate near 1.5, where bigger fractions actually favour tumour over the rectum and bladder beside it.
steps.say: Alpha beta ratio measures fractionation sensitivity: tumours and early tissues sit high near ten, while late tissues like cord sit near two to three and are spared by small fractions. Prostate near one point five lets bigger fractions favour tumour over rectum and bladder.

Late tissues such as spinal cord sit low, near 2 to 3, and are spared by small fractions. Hypofractionation exploits a low tumour ratio. steps.say: Alpha beta ratio measures how much fraction size matters. Tumours and early reacting tissues, near 10, repair little between doses. Spinal cord and other late tissues, near 2 to 3, are spared by small fractions. Prostate cancer near 1.5 can take larger fractions while rectum and bladder are relatively spared.

steps.title: Oxygen enhancement and LET
steps.tx: **Oxygen enhancement ratio** compares doses needed for the same kill without and with oxygen, reaching about 2.5 to 3 for standard low LET photons, because oxygen fixes DNA radical damage into permanent breaks. High LET radiation like neutrons and carbon ions barely needs oxygen, with ratios near 1, and packs ionisations densely for a higher relative biological effectiveness. That physics is the sales case for particle therapy in hypoxic, radioresistant tumours.
steps.say: Oxygen enhancement ratio compares doses needed without and with oxygen, reaching about two point five to three for photons, because oxygen fixes DNA damage permanently. High LET particles barely need oxygen, with ratios near one, and pack ionisations densely for higher biological effectiveness.

steps.title: Bergonie Tribondeau law
steps.tx: **Bergonie Tribondeau law** states that radiosensitivity rises with mitotic rate and proliferative future and falls with differentiation, explaining why lymphocytes, spermatogonia, marrow and gut lining die first while neurons and muscle endure. Lymphocytes break the mitotic rule by dying in interphase at tiny doses, the famous exception examiners plant. The law ranks tissue sensitivity for every acute syndrome and protection question in this module.

steps.title: Radiosensitisers and protectors
steps.tx: **Radiosensitisers** widen the therapeutic gap from the tumour side: concurrent cisplatin adds DNA crosslinks in head and neck and cervical cancers, oxygen and nimorazole attack hypoxia, and hyperthermia disables repair enzymes. Protectors widen it from the normal side, amifostine scavenging radicals in salivary glands being the textbook example. Every combined modality protocol in the clinical lessons is one of these radiobiology levers pulled deliberately.
steps.say: Radiosensitisers widen the therapeutic gap from the tumour side: cisplatin adds DNA crosslinks, nimorazole attacks hypoxia and heat disables repair. Protectors like amifostine widen it from the normal side. Every combined protocol in the clinical lessons is one of these radiobiology levers pulled deliberately.
